proposed.text: A candidate's LEA scores are: Design 75%, Building Science 68%, Professional Practice 82%, History 48%. Does this candidate pass?

options.text: Yes, because the weighted average exceeds 70%, which is the general passing criterion for the ALE
No, because the History score falls below the 50% minimum requirement
Yes, with a conditional pass pending History retake, which is not a standard provision in ALE regulations
No, because Building Science is below 70%, which is not a disqualifying factor if the overall average is sufficient

rationale.a: Ignores the mandatory no-subject-below-50% safeguard; weighted average alone is insufficient.
rationale.c: Misrepresents the law; conditional passes do not exist; failure of the 50% floor on any subject bars passing outright.
rationale.d: Confuses the floor threshold; the law requires 50% minimum per subject, not 70%; Building Science at 68% meets the requirement.
rationale.correct: Even if the weighted average exceeds 70%, the dual-threshold requirement mandates that no individual subject may fall below 50%. History at 48% violates this floor, making the candidate ineligible to pass regardless of overall average.
rationale.takeaway: Dual threshold blocks passing: any subject below 50% fails the candidate, even with 70%+ weighted average.
